newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM holds cabinet meeting in poor province.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM holds cabinet meeting in poor province.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh held his weekly cabinet meeting in this northern town on Tuesday in a bid to show sympathy with concerns raised by the area's poor villagers.
After the meeting, which he dubbed "the hardship cabinet meeting," the premier pledged to find quick solutions to longstanding land disputes between the government and poor villagers.

"This government is the government of the poor so we will do all to solve the problem of the poor. That's why we came to you to meet you here," Chavalit told a cheering crowd of about 10,000 villagers at the meeting venue in the province of Nakorn Ratchasima, about 300 km (183 miles) from the capital Bangkok.
"I decided to hold the meeting here because I want cabinet members to get on-the-spot information and to see how difficult is the life you lead here," he said.
Some cabinet ministers used to air-conditioned rooms complained about the heat and humidity, but the five-hour meeting went ahead as scheduled.

Land disputes figure high among the many problems of the area's poor, who have faced off against the government over the frequent encroachment by farmland-seeking villagers onto state land, natural parks and forests.

"The meeting has resolved that you be allowed to stay where you are and the government will work out legal measures to facilitate your right to stay on the plots of land where you are now," Chavalit added.

Historically the least-developed region of Thailand, the northeast provinces have been left even further behind by the country's recent economic development, which has centred on Bangkok and triggered mass migrations to the capital from the provinces.

About 15,000 poor villagers, mostly from the northeastern provinces, have been camping near Government House in Bangkok for three months in a marathon protest to demand government help in resolving their problems.
They are seeking release from debts owed to state-owned banks, higher prices for their farm produce and settlement of land disputes with the government.

The well-organised group, led by a movement called the Assembly of the Poor, on April 8th blocked most exits from Government House after Chavalit and some ministers finished their weekly cabinet meeting there.

"The resolution at today's cabinet meeting also covers those people who face land disputes and are now staying in front of the Government House," government spokesman Warrathep Rattanakorn told reporters.
But Sunai Jullapongstorn, deputy government spokesman and a member of parliament for the Chart Pattana Party, questioned the usefulness of Tuesday's meeting.
"I still have doubts about the outcome of the meeting. I don't know of one meeting which has brought any fruitful result to villagers," he said.
